title: Trust assigned by connection origin: an unauthenticated fetch aimed at the server itself becomes loopback, and the server signs its own token to the attacker
index_line: T-0071 · AUTH_DECISION · junk-token SSRF to 127.0.0.1 unguards the loopback-only API; a forged plugin call fetches a 127.0.0.1-prefixed host and the auto-attached owner token leaks · cpp · corroborated
invariant_violated: Requests from loopback are the server talking to itself, so they were trusted without a token. But anyone who can point one of the server's own outbound requests at 127.0.0.1 makes the server talk to itself — and the framework attaches the owner's admin token to any outbound URL that merely starts with the string http://127.0.0.1.

mechanism.does: an internet attacker sends a request to the timeline endpoint with any junk token and a full URL in the protocol parameter
the server POSTs to the attacker-chosen destination — aiming it at its own 127.0.0.1 makes the request originate from loopback
the loopback-only plugin-management API accepts the request because it came from the server itself
the searchOne identifier value is not neutralized: attacker parameters forge a call to another plugin function with attacker-supplied arguments

the forged fetch targets a hostname beginning 127.0.0.1. (attacker wildcard DNS); the server sees the prefix, auto-attaches the owner's admin token, and DNS resolves the name to the attacker — the token is exfiltrated

source.http.request.value: the timeline/searchOne request parameters — junk tokens accepted, full URLs and identifiers passed through

guard.none.value: the origin classifier is not forged — it is legitimately satisfied; nothing asks who directed the server to talk to itself

sink.http.request.value: the two server-side fetches: to itself (origin reclassification) and to the 127.0.0.1-prefixed host (token exfil)

encoding.url.value: payload shape: full URL in the protocol parameter; identifier injection in searchOne; 127.0.0.1.<attacker-domain> for a prefix-respecting, attacker-resolving hostname

preconditions.expr: the media server port is reachable from the attacker's position (frequently internet-exposed for remote streaming)
the timeline endpoint accepts any token value and a full URL (pre-1.43.3.10861)
trust is decided by connection origin, and token auto-attachment is keyed on a 127.0.0.1 string prefix rather than the resolved address

success: the server POSTs to an attacker-chosen URL with no valid token (out-of-band callback)
a loopback-origin request reaches the loopback-only plugin API and invokes a plugin function with attacker parameters
an outbound fetch to a 127.0.0.1-prefixed DNS name carries the owner's admin token to the attacker — full server takeover material
failure_like: 1.43.3.10861 and later reject external URLs / neutralize the identifier / attach tokens only after resolution
the port is not exposed beyond the LAN
false_positive: plain SSRF to an external host is T-0003's cousin but not this record — the violated invariant is origin-based trust plus prefix-keyed token attachment
a callback to the attacker proves only the fetch leg; the loopback reclassification and the token exfil are separate observables

hazards: every service that classifies trust by connection origin (loopback, RFC1918, cluster-internal): anything that lets an outsider aim one of the service's own requests at it reclassifies that request as trusted
prefix-matching an address string instead of the resolved IP is the exfil half — wildcard DNS services resolve the 'safe' prefix to the attacker
pairs with T-0037 for the landing: the owner token unlocks the preference-write that drops an executable into the codecs directory (the full chain to shell)
the fix must cover both halves: restrict the outbound-fetch surface and key token attachment on the resolved address, not the string
non_transfers: services that require tokens on all interfaces including loopback
deployments where the port is unreachable from the attacker's network position

evidence.target: Plex Media Server < 1.43.3.10861 (CVE-2026-96652 / 96654 / 96655 of the plex2shell chain; T-0037 records the CVE-2026-96656 landing stage)

provenance.author: zmain
provenance.corroborates: the full chain: timeline SSRF with any token value to 127.0.0.1; loopback reclassification; searchOne identifier injection forging plugin calls; token auto-attach on the 127.0.0.1 string prefix with wildcard-DNS exfil; CVSS 9.8
